name: Revisionist Maximalism
summary: Revisionist Maximalism was the radical wing of Revisionist Zionism, founded around 1930 by Abba Ahimeir, Uri Zvi Greenberg and Yehoshua Yeivin after the 1929 riots. It demanded a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan won by revolt against British rule, rejected Jabotinsky's restraint toward Arabs and British, and wanted the movement run on the Italian Fascist model with Jabotinsky as dictator. It was militarist, anti-socialist, anti-liberal and framed by secular-messianic readings of Jewish history, and it collapsed in 1933 after the Arlosoroff affair.
scope: The Maximalist bloc and its clandestine arm Brit HaBirionim (1930-1933), as set out by Ahimeir, Greenberg and Yeivin and in the Hazit HaAm press, with Ahimeir's thought (Spenglerian, anti-democratic, revolutionary) as the core. It excludes Jabotinsky's own liberal-democratic Revisionism, later Likud politics and Lehi/Irgun, though some members joined them later. The sources document politics, militarism and nationalism well but say little on economics or social issues, so many answers on those are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ahimeir's writings on economics are mostly about Jewish labor and self-reliance, so there is no documented view on state health care; a fascist-modelled state could go either way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The group broke strikes in 1932-33 and attacked Labour Zionist union power, so a state-set wage floor is inferred to be unattractive to them.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ahimeir rejected liberalism and was drawn to Fascist state direction, though he was not a planner; inferred mild disagreement that markets beat government.

public-ownership.rationale: Ahimeir left Marxism and socialism behind but favored a strong nationalist state; no documented view on nationalizing utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Maximalists accused liberal Zionists of serving only the middle class, but no tax policy is documented.

unions-good.rationale: The Maximalists supplied strike-breakers in 1932-33 and fought the Histadrut-led Labour movement, which points to hostility toward class-based unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Fascist-style nationalism subordinates property to the nation, and Ahimeir held no liberal rights doctrine; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No documented position; a Fascist-modelled order would subordinate business to the nation but the group never set out an economic program here.

cut-welfare.rationale: No documented position on welfare; the Maximalists stressed national solidarity, which cuts both ways.

worker-ownership.rationale: They rejected socialism and class politics for national unity, so collective worker ownership is inferred as unwelcome.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A militarist, authoritarian movement in a period of Arab violence would accept security measures for the nation; inferred, not documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Authoritarian, disciplinarian nationalism suggests disapproval; the sources do not address drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Their own press was provocative and they rejected liberal norms; speech restriction aimed at nationalist agitation would be opposed.

strong-leader.rationale: At the 1932 Revisionist conference the Maximalists demanded that Jabotinsky's prestige be raised to that of a dictator, per Bergamin and Wikipedia.

state-harmful.rationale: The group wanted a strong, even dictatorial, nationalist order and a Jewish state, the opposite of anti-statism.

limit-guns.rationale: The movement was militarist and wanted a fighting national guard, so strict civilian gun limits are unlikely to appeal; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Strongly militarist, rejected pacifism, and wanted a military academy named for Jabotinsky, as Wikipedia reports.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Authoritarian-national moral discipline implies disapproval; no sources address it.

decide-locally.rationale: Integralist, one-party, leader-centered nationalism calls for centralised national unity rather than local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: Disciplinarian ethos suggests punishment over rehabilitation; inferred only.

traditional-family.rationale: Spenglerian, völkisch nationalism favors family and national continuity, but the sources do not discuss family policy.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from nationalist conservatism of the period; not discussed in the sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from völkisch nationalism and national-growth concerns; not documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ahimeir saw Zionism as secular but drew on prophets, zealots and Sicarii as national history; religion served the nation, so split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue of the period; their stress on national interest over liberal equality implies disagreement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; völkisch nationalism leans toward fixed natural roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Revival of Jewish national history, with Second Temple zealots and Sicarii as models, was central to Ahimeir's cultural-historical outlook.

gradual-change.rationale: Ahimeir was a self-described revolutionary who sought revolt against Britain and rejected moderate Zionist gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The aim was a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan built by Jewish immigration; reduction of Jewish immigration is opposed, though other immigration was not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They rejected internationalism and diplomacy through the League and the Mandate, preferring national political action.

free-trade.rationale: Jewish economic self-reliance was promoted but trade policy is not documented.

nation-first.rationale: Maximalists rejected internationalism and humanism and put the Jewish nation's liberation above all other considerations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Their nationalist focus is on national interest; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Rejected internationalism; an integral nationalism has no place for open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Spengler-influenced but pro-national-strength; no documented view on environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: A 1930s movement never addressed climate; a state-power ethos would favor action but nationalist growth priorities cut against it, so split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Spengler's view of technology as part of civilization's decline influenced Ahimeir, but he was no technophobe; unclear.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the group's emphasis on national strength and self-reliance, held at low confidence.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bergamin presents Ahimeir as a revolutionary who coined 'revolutionary Zionism' and called for revolt to win a Jewish state.

experts-over-public.rationale: No documented view; they favored rule by a leader and order rather than either public or experts.

central-planning.rationale: No documented economic planning; a Fascist-modelled state might plan, but the group's economics were thin.

socialized-markets.rationale: They rejected socialism and its public ownership as class politics; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Neither the Maximalist press nor the scholarship mentions land taxation, and nothing in their nationalist principles favors one side.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Maximalists attacked liberal Zionists as middle-class but left no tax program, so no direction can be inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from rejection of socialism and emphasis on national labor and discipline.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Jewish economic independence and self-reliance were promoted; protection of national industry is a plausible implication.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Modelled on Italian Fascism and promoting national economic self-reliance; direction by the state is inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No documented position on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: They rejected communism and socialism outright.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from favoring a strong state; not discussed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The group wanted an Italian Fascist modus operandi, whose economic model was corporatist, but Maximalists did not publish a corporatist program.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wikipedia reports a one-party order and dictatorship as the group's goal, and Ahimeir wanted an Orden rather than a mass party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Ahimeir saw monarchy versus republic as an obsolete contest replaced by dictatorship versus democracy; he did not champion monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Bergamin documents Ahimeir's Spenglerian contempt for liberal democracy, and Wikipedia says the group rejected it.

direct-votes.rationale: Mass plebiscitary democracy sits badly with their dictatorship demand; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: They rejected socialism and class-based politics in favor of an integral nation.

right-to-secede.rationale: National integralism and territorial maximalism oppose breakaway rights; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Elitist leader-cult and dictatorship ideas imply some are suited to rule; Ahimeir's Spenglerian view of great men supports this.

political-violence-never.rationale: They rejected pacifism and the Sicarii-style fighters were their models, though direct endorsement of terror is contested in the scholarship.

war-builds-character.rationale: Strongly militarist and anti-pacifist; Ahimeir admired military virtue and the 'conquer or die' motto.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ahimeir viewed Zionism as secular but used religious motifs for nationalism; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ahimeir treated Zionism as a secular territorial phenomenon, so scriptural law is not his goal.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-centric militarist movement would reject privatised defense.

military-superiority.rationale: Strong militarism and a fighting national guard imply insisting on strength against rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bergamin places Ahimeir within Jewish völkisch nationalism; the Jewish state was meant to be a Jewish national home.

class-struggle-history.rationale: They rejected socialism and communism and emphasized national solidarity over class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rejected socialism and egalitarian politics in favor of nation and hierarchy.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Revisionists held that Zionist colonization must proceed regardless of native opposition, per the Iron Wall; Arab authority was not accepted.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Their anti-British line was against Mandate, not about reparations; inferred disagreement.

civilizational-union.rationale: Their focus was a Jewish national state, not union with other nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective national interest dominates; no documented view on personal self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Integral nationalism of the Fascist type subordinates the individual to the nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Their outlook was nation- and history-centered, valuing the land as homeland rather than nature for itself; inferred only.

limit-population.rationale: A movement intent on Jewish demographic strength would not limit growth; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Spenglerian cultural pessimism influenced Ahimeir, but no documented rejection of industry; split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Spengler, Ahimeir's main influence, saw technics as a symptom of civilizational decline, while state-building favored progress; split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from disciplinarian, tradition-and-history-minded nationalism.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; authoritarian orientation implies state access.

restore-past-order.rationale: They looked to ancient Zealots and Sicarii for inspiration but sought a new state and revolution, not restoration of a lost social order.

direct-action.rationale: Brit HaBirionim staged demonstrations, census boycott and Western Wall shofar blowing and Ahimeir favored revolt over diplomacy.

means-match-ends.rationale: Revolutionary pragmatism: Bergamin says Fascism was merely a modus operandi for revolution; means not tied to ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Spenglerian civilization theory and state-building aims reject it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: They rejected communism and socialism outright, including its utopian aims of abolishing the division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The group rejected communism and socialism, and put national unity above egalitarian distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist formula they would reject along with socialism, though they promoted national economic self-reliance, hence only mild.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Ahimeir had abandoned Marxism and condemned class struggle; he saw labor and capital as parts of the nation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The group rejected communism, Marxism and class rule, and wanted national dictatorship instead.

collective-farming.rationale: Rejected Labour Zionist collectivism as socialist; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory of imperialism is rejected; no documented view.

taxation-theft.rationale: A movement seeking a strong dictatorial state and national mobilization would reject the view that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: They rejected liberalism and wanted state authority to enforce national discipline well beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: They rejected liberalism and put the nation above the individual.

conscription.rationale: Strong militarism and a national-guard ethos favored mass service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Integral nationalism; no support for exit as check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Authoritarian nationalism does not treat citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberal freedom language was rejected; inferred that national duty, not material means of action, defined freedom for them.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source records Maximalist views on universities or media power; they attacked official Zionist leaders instead.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Spenglerian culture theory, not biological race science, shaped Ahimeir; not documented.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist and Fascist-style organic order implied; Ahimeir wanted an order rather than a parliamentary party.

total-state.rationale: Wikipedia says the group sought a state on fascist principles; I take a mild yes since the fully totalising state is not documented in detail.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ahimeir and Greenberg preached a secular-messianic national revolution against the Diaspora and its passivity.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Maximalists accepted the Revisionist demand for a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan and Greenberg called for a Kingdom of Israel.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Leader cult and an Orden bound by loyalty to the leader are documented, but feudal oaths are not.

bound-labor.rationale: Not a feature of the program; modern nationalist movement.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Spenglerian relativism about civilizations points one way, their claim to historical truth another; split.

universal-morality.rationale: Spenglerian cultural relativism about civilizations influenced Ahimeir, implying skepticism about universals.

single-common-good.rationale: Integral nationalism assumes one national interest above class divisions.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The central demand: a Jewish state in the Land of Israel, called for by Brit HaBirionim before other groups.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The aim was bringing Jews to a Jewish state in the Land of Israel, negating Galut life geographically and spiritually.

revive-national-language.rationale: They were Hebrew-culture nationalists and Ahimeir wanted integration into Hebrew society.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from rejection of socialism and Fascist hierarchical model.

school-vouchers.rationale: No documented education-finance position; nationalist indoctrination aims could cut either way.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No documented fiscal views; the sources are about politics, violence and national identity.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rejected liberalism; political freedom was not their goal.

rule-by-example.rationale: Heroic exemplars like the Sicarii and a leader cult favored example, but not documented as against law.

national-self-determination.rationale: National liberation of the Jewish people in their own state was their cause.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Spenglerian and messianic emphasis on will and destiny over rational liberalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from a nation-first outlook that would favor benefits for the national community.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Their Jewish labor and self-reliance emphasis suggests favoring work obligations; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Integral nationalism opposed class struggle and condemned liberal Zionists for serving only the middle class instead of the nation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: They revered historical heritage and national memory.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-British but not documented as seeking a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Their Jewish Labor stress favored national, not international, workers' organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the Fascist-modelled, militarist, völkisch outlook; the sources do not discuss gender.

ban-interest.rationale: Not an issue they raised; mildly rejected as an economic restriction at odds with a nationalist-capitalist mix.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Their program was a Jewish national state, not racial classification law; inferred mild disagreement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Ahimeir left Marxism and treated class analysis as divisive of the nation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; national self-sufficiency would favor domestic energy, but the group never addressed it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Wikipedia says they wanted Palestine's population integrated into Hebrew society.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of this kind is not part of Maximalist ideas; their grievance was with the British and official Zionist leaders.

proportional-representation.rationale: They despised party-parliamentary democracy, so a PR system is not something they would favor.

national-mission.rationale: Secular messianism implies a special Jewish national mission, but spreading its government abroad is not stated.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not documented; nationalist movement unlikely to endorse.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They attacked official Zionist leaders as collaborators with Britain.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No source addresses eugenics for the Maximalists; inferred mildly negative from their Jewish-revival and not racial-biological focus.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A militarist movement that wanted a stronger army and rejected havlagah would not hold its forces to account for past killings.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They sought a strong dictatorial order, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement's nationalism concerned Jewish national revival; no source gives a view on intermarriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ahimeir considered Arabs less evolved in earlier articles and rejected liberalism and humanism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate they did not join; they rejected socialism altogether, so they disagree with its premise.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Revisionists acknowledged colonization but denied it was unjust; Jabotinsky says Zionism is moral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Integral nationalist state implies one law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not a Maximalist issue; no source speaks to it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Secular nationalists had no stake in religious cattle laws; inferred mild disagreement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ahimeir was secular yet used biblical heroes as national history, so religious instruction in schools is a split question.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate they never joined; no view can be inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rejection of liberal democracy and call for dictatorship; Jabotinsky said colonization would proceed regardless of Arab consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Their stress on national economic independence makes a surplus-seeking policy plausible; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented; some Revisionists discussed transfer but not in these sources.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They rejected pacifism and Jabotinsky's Iron Wall approves force to proceed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Spenglerian struggle between cultures shaped Ahimeir's worldview.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A movement that itself flouted British Mandate rules and sought revolution would oppose banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-British freedom struggle, but not republican theory.

separated-powers.rationale: They wanted dictatorship and a leader cult, the opposite of checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Ahimeir wanted a disciplined Orden and clandestine vanguard group, though for nationalism not class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: They rejected socialism and class framing, preferring national over class priorities.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Anachronistic British policy with no counterpart in their program.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: They supplied strike-breakers in 1932-33 labour disputes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A movement seeking Jewish demographic growth would not blame population; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Integral nationalism implies unity needed; weak inference.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hostile to democracy and to egalitarian selection, they wanted rule by a leader and order.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian logic of a dictatorship-seeking group suggests acceptance; no source states it directly.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No economic-policy documents; nationalist statism might support it, liberal-capitalist side against, so split.

party-controls-media.rationale: One-party model implies control; the group ran its own press, but control of all media is not documented.

party-commands-army.rationale: Under a one-party or leader-dominated order the movement commands the military; inferred from the Fascist model.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from integral nationalism, though Jewish immigration itself was to be encouraged.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A socialist-democratic measure they would not support.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Ahimeir's Orden concept demanded strict discipline in a leader-led movement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Maximalists rejected internationalism and wanted full national sovereignty for a Jewish state.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Leader as dictator implies command of the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to a Jewish nationalist movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: Ahimeir regarded Zionism as a secular, territorial movement, not a religiously ruled one.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Their nationalism and militarism opposed the defeatist, class-first stance of this socialist slogan.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian national-discipline outlook; the sources do not discuss censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Dictatorship demand implies no term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Opposed to democratic checks on a leader.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: They opposed reliance on Britain but did not discuss alliances in general.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No source mentions it; inferred disagreement as an extreme egalitarian measure.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militarism and national guard idea (Betar) lean to armed citizenry; professional army abolition is not documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Spenglerian anti-city motif is possible but not documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Their territorial claim treats the land on both banks of the Jordan as one national territory, split by the 1922 White Paper.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ahimeir himself was a Vienna-educated doctor of history, but attacked the Zionist establishment; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Spengler's morphology of independent cultures influenced Ahimeir, though he judged Arabs less evolved.

death-penalty.rationale: Militarist, harsh outlook; Ahimeir was himself tried for conspiracy; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from conservative, nation-disciplinary educational aims; not documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular outlook with academic leaders like Ahimeir (PhD), so unlikely to favor it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from disciplinarian, anti-bourgeois-decadence outlook; not documented.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Völkisch Jewish nationalism implies descent-based membership; the right of return was the aim.

minority-language-support.rationale: Wikipedia says they wanted the population integrated into Hebrew society, so minority-language support is unlikely.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Integralist state demanding unity would not grant exemptions; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: They rejected liberalism and prized discipline, a leader and national unity over individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anachronistic and outside any Maximalist concern.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Maximalists wanted political independence first and promoted economic self-reliance; no sources show a view on property transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: They rejected parliamentary democracy and sought leader-centered rule.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Authoritarian logic: they would accept restricting freedoms for national goals; not stated directly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nation-first outlook suggests rejection of a global duty; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic, but their emphasis on military self-reliance suggests approval.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Ahimeir wanted a leader-dictator, but no documented mechanism for choosing him; plebiscitary and appointed routes both fit.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The sources never touch monetary institutions, and no position follows from the principles.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Maximalists demanded a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan and Jabotinsky's Iron Wall rejected deals before Arab acceptance.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Integral nationalism subordinates private interest to the nation; economic doctrine is thinly documented.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ahimeir saw Bolshevism as Russian nationalism, not as state capitalism; the question is outside their debate.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

collective-defense.rationale: Anachronistic; they opposed reliance on Britain but there is no view on alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Maximalists claim the whole Land of Israel as the Jewish national home, so they reject the idea.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Ahimeir's Zionism was secular, yet he drew on religious symbols; no documented policy toward clergy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: They wanted the leader to be head of the movement and a dictator, not a neutral figure.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Militarist integral nationalism would back force to keep the nation whole; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: They wanted a unitary, ideologically uniform national order.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Cult of the leader was proposed, but divine descent contradicts their secular framework.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No tax policy is documented and no principle points one way.

character-from-environment.rationale: Spenglerian and völkisch thinking stresses innate national character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Dictatorship and the Duce model imply a ruler not constrained by parliamentary law.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; Spenglerian expansion theme versus no stated view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: They wanted dictatorship over mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Wikipedia and Bergamin both report the Maximalist demand for a cult of the leader, with Jabotinsky as Duce.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: They rejected socialism and class struggle both; mild disagreement.

land-redistribution.rationale: They rejected socialism and Labour Zionist collectivism; mild disagreement inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Revisionist view in the Iron Wall rejects Arab claims to prevent a Jewish majority.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Their claim rested on Jewish historical and religious ties, not on co-nationals abroad, but the logic is similar.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Ahimeir's secular nationalism had no place for punishing religious exit.

women-must-cover.rationale: A secular nationalist movement would not impose religious dress law.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Their focus was a Jewish nation-state, not pan-ethnic unions; mild disagreement inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Revisionism and Maximalism demanded a Jewish state, and Jabotinsky's Iron Wall rejected equal-rights minority formulas as the aim.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Maximalists rejected Diaspora existence and sought a Jewish state in Palestine.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Ahimeir broke with Marxism and, following Spengler, saw history as driven by will, culture and national destiny rather than by modes of production.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They rejected liberal constraints but also democratic majorities; a dictator was the aim.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Promoted Jewish economic independence and self-reliance, though not a closed imperial bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Secular-messianic duty to the nation resembles moral incentives; no economics documented.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Brit HaBirionim was a small clandestine group aiming to spark revolt, and Ahimeir viewed himself as a revolutionary vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: They rejected aristocracy-style hierarchy in favor of national movement leadership and had a revolutionary bent; weak inference.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Ahimeir's cultural-historical conception of the Jewish nation put national history at the center.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ahimeir considered Arabs less evolved, though a formal tutelage doctrine is not documented.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ahimeir instructed in the Betar Leadership Training School and sought national indoctrination of youth.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not documented; they rejected Marxism but offered no theory of capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not relevant to a movement aimed at a new state.

delink-world-market.rationale: Promoted Jewish economic independence, but no sources describe a break with world markets.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist concept rejected along with socialism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Jewish-labor campaigns imply economic preference for co-nationals, while state authority would be strong; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rejection of liberal constitutionalism and of individual rights limiting national authority.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No relevant position; they opposed the Mandate but on other grounds.

elective-rulers.rationale: They wanted a dictator rather than elected rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Totally opposed to veto politics; they sought dictatorship and unity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: They resisted the British but championed an unchecked leader of their own.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rejected parliamentary democracy and sought dictatorship.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No documented view; national solidarity might imply duty, but the sources do not say.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Maximalism was an activist revolutionary movement that urged political action and sacrifice.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory idea not addressed in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian idea they did not address.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory idea outside their framework.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-party question outside their scope.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Promoted economic self-reliance for the Jewish community.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Maximalists rejected the 1922 separation of Transjordan from the Land of Israel and sought both banks.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Revisionist doctrine asserted Jewish colonization regardless of native Arab opposition and aimed at a Jewish state.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: They were self-declared fascists, though they later opposed Nazi Germany and boycotted its goods.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Split: Ahimeir hated communism but organised against Nazi swastikas in 1933, though he was himself a fascist.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ahimeir's Spenglerian view treats each civilization as having its own forms and rejects imported Western liberal democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Strong militarism; the army as national guard.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from conservative gender outlook; not discussed.

office-by-exam.rationale: Ahimeir was an academic, but the sources show no view on how state posts should be filled.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Jewish economic self-reliance implies protecting national economic control.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from conservative nationalist social outlook.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Opposed to democratic accountability of the leader.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not documented; Zionist national land ideas were mixed.

single-official-language.rationale: Wikipedia says they wanted the population integrated into Hebrew society, and Hebrew revival was central.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Their cause was Jewish land redemption and national control of the land; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from rejection of liberal egalitarianism.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Spenglerian cultural pessimism and anti-bourgeois attitude suggest it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The sources give no view on foreign policy toward hostile governments; the group's own insurgent stance was against the Mandate.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Question about bloc politics outside their scope.

corporate-influence.rationale: The sources show no Maximalist view on lobbying or corporate power.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A movement aiming at a Jewish majority would welcome growth; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: No source addresses local limits on property purchases.

job-guarantee.rationale: Their 'Jewish labor' stance favored employing Jews, but a state job guarantee is not documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: They disbelieved in liberal democracy and in pacifist internationalism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Disciplinarian loyalty to the order and leader.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from militarist, power-focused outlook; not documented.

industrial-unions.rationale: They opposed the labor federation; no view on union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not documented about any minority in this context.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from conservative nationalist social outlook.

public-access-to-information.rationale: An authoritarian leader-led movement is unlikely to favor transparency rights.

local-production.rationale: No source addresses local production; they did stress national economic self-reliance only.

informal-organisation.rationale: Ahimeir wanted a disciplined hierarchical Orden led by a leader, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Rejected internationalism and the Mandate authorities' legitimacy over Jewish national claims.

religious-nation.rationale: Ahimeir treated Zionism as secular territorial nationalism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Maximalists fought against the British Mandate and rejected Zionist deference to Britain.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Centralist integral nationalism opposes regional retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist formula; they rejected communism but this specific point is not addressed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rejected communism and was disillusioned with Bolshevism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are not covered by any source on the Maximalists.

religion-illusion.rationale: He treated prophets and zealots as historical realities and used religious language for nationalism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Bergamin calls him a bourgeois revolutionary, but there is no stated view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist claim, rejected with socialism.

socialized-care.rationale: They rejected socialism and its collectivization of household tasks.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Hebrew revival nationalists favored linguistic purity; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not documented; Revisionist hostility to the Mandate terms, hence weak inference.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Rejected socialism and its cooperative collectivism.

majority-settlement.rationale: Revisionists sought Jewish settlement toward a Jewish majority.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Their Fascist-modelled integral nationalism claimed a third way beyond liberal capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Maximalists grounded their claim to the whole Land of Israel on Jewish history and the Bible, treating prophets and zealots as historical realities.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The group campaigned against Nazi Germany in 1933, removing swastikas from consulates and boycotting German goods.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; conservatism points one way, secularism another.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Dictatorship goals and strike-breaking; Maximalists sought a one-party order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Secular movement would not punish blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement sought a Jewish state, not an imperial metropole; no source discusses colonial economics, so mild disagreement is inferred from the nationalist-liberation framing.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not their ideology; hostile to the Arabs in the 1929 context.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Their movement was secular and fought the Mandate on national, not religious-law, grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: They rejected democratic politics for leader-centered order.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: They rejected socialism, humanism and liberalism that underlie this view.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed in the sources; nothing in their principles settles it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ahimeir rejected labels and sought a revolutionary third course.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept they rejected along with Marxism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Maximalist hostility was aimed at the British and the Arab leadership in the Yishuv context, with no documented claims about Islam and the West.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No documented view; secular outlook might favor it but not stated.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic workplace-law question with no relevance to the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rejected liberal and socialist middle courses for an integral national model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: They rejected pacifism and demanded a military academy, so they strongly oppose it.

rich-first.rationale: No source addresses development sequencing or unequal growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: They opposed reliance on Britain but the sources show no view on great-power blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ahimeir saw monarchy versus republic as obsolete; he wanted a dictator, not a dynasty.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic international-finance question; no source applies.

property-franchise.rationale: They sought dictatorship and not a limited franchise; mild disagreement.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not their ideology; they favored dominance of national will over nature and admired military conquest.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: They ran their own press, Hazit HaAm, but did not make this critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: A dictatorship-oriented movement would favor leader discretion over standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Not documented; nationalist rather than racial legal program.

open-government-data.rationale: An authoritarian leader-led movement is unlikely to favor open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A secular movement with no documented view.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: They called a boycott of German goods but not of local minorities; not documented.

citizens-assembly.rationale: They rejected democracy and its deliberative forms.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Ahimeir secularized and nationalized religious motifs, but did not propose reinterpretation of religious law.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: They did not prize liberty, and their critique of liberal Zionists was about middle-class interests.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: They used religious figures as national heroes, so state atheism is unlikely.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A militarist, order-oriented movement seeking a strong state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Rejected arrangements that would limit Jewish national rule; Iron Wall says no voluntary agreement.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: No source addresses poor relief or the role of charity.

term-limits.rationale: They wanted a leader as dictator without limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: They rejected democracy and its direct forms.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Ahimeir's Zionism was secular and the sources do not discuss religious office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: No source discusses marriage; conservative outlook points one way, secular modernity another.

abolish-ip.rationale: No source addresses patents or copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ahimeir led Betar's leadership school, and the movement's aesthetic included uniforms and military drill.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The group opposed British power in Palestine but nothing is documented on foreign bases generally.

recognise-genocide.rationale: No source records a Maximalist view on recognition of past genocides.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Their Jewish labor ethos prized work; this is a weak inference.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: They rejected pacifism and Jabotinsky's havlagah was too restrained for them.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ahimeir's cultural-historical conception connected Sicarii and zealots to modern Zionism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Sicarii and zealot heroes of the Scroll of the Sicarii were models; sacrifice for the nation was central.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maximalist rhetoric was imbued with secular-Messianic overtones.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: They demanded a Jewish state and negated the Diaspora spiritually and geographically.

culture-before-state.rationale: Political liberation came first; they criticized cultural Zionism.

god-not-male.rationale: Ahimeir's secular Zionism leaves no stated view on theological language.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Maximalists promoted Jewish labor and economic independence.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Their territorial program sought one state on both banks of the Jordan for the Jewish people.

independent-unions.rationale: Strike-breaking against the Histadrut shows hostility to labour-union independence claims; they wanted national organisation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: They rejected socialism, so the test of working-class power is irrelevant.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No source addresses local utilities or hospitals.

second-chamber.rationale: No documented view; inferred from rejection of parliamentary forms.

municipal-property.rationale: They rejected socialism and collective ownership.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic regulatory question; no source applies.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

person-over-state.rationale: They rejected liberalism and individualism in favor of the nation.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

dense-cities.rationale: No source addresses urban form, though Spengler's critique of the metropolis influenced Ahimeir.

racial-group-interests.rationale: No documented view; their focus was national rather than racial.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Maximalists rejected havlagah and wanted proactive militarism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Hebrew revival mattered to them, but the sources do not say language alone defines nationhood.

communal-electorates.rationale: Opposed, since they rejected electoral politics and sought a unitary state.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: They saw Britain as anti-Zionist and hostile.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Ahimeir's circle wrote almost nothing on environmental or resource policy, so no position can be inferred from a militarist, state-building programme.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the Maximalists' messianic, history-centred nationalism, which treats the present as a link to future national generations; no source addresses the Earth directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the movement's fascist-modelled militarism and cult of force, which sits badly with giving care and nonviolence more public weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Maximalists demanded armed revolt against the British and a Jewish military force, and rejected Jabotinsky's restraint, so cutting armaments contradicts their core approach.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from their conspiratorial, clandestine tactics (Brit HaBirionim) and admiration for Fascist-style leadership, which favour discretion over open treaty-making.

capital-controls.rationale: Their sources are anti-socialist but also fascist-inspired and nation-first, and say nothing specific on capital movements, so adherents could go either way.

missingStatements.text: A national movement seeking independence should answer attacks with force rather than restraint.
missingStatements.rationale: Maximalists explicitly rejected Jabotinsky's havlagah (defensive restraint) toward Arabs and British in favor of a proactive, militaristic approach.

missingStatements.text: A people under foreign colonial rule should fight the ruling power rather than rely on diplomacy with it.
missingStatements.rationale: Unlike Jabotinsky's diplomacy with Britain, the Maximalists fought the Mandate government ideologically and actively, seeing it as hostile to their cause.

notes: Scholars dispute how far Ahimeir's fascism was doctrine versus revolutionary method (Bergamin), and the claim that the group mainly targeted British and Zionist rivals rather than Arabs is flagged as needing citation on Wikipedia. Jabotinsky himself did not adopt the Maximalist program. No primary text by Ahimeir was opened; his views are taken from Bergamin's quotations and Wikipedia, and the Iron Wall stands for the shared Revisionist base.
